harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built and deployed a small SQLite-backed CGI "inventory application" (add/list items) served by httpd on node1's TCP port 8181, with SELinux/mandatory access control kept in enforcing mode throughout. Configured semanage port to label 8181 as http_port_t (so the confined httpd_t domain is permitted to bind it), set correct file contexts (httpd_sys_script_exec_t for the CGI script, httpd_sys_rw_content_t for the writable data directory), opened the port in firewalld, verified end-to-end functionality (GET renders inventory table, POST adds an item and persists it), then executed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline, issued systemctl reboot with the ack returned before disconnect, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and re-verified SELinux enforcing, httpd active/enabled and confined under httpd_t, port 8181 listening, firewall rule persisted, and the previously stored inventory item ("Widget", qty 42) still present.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (AlmaLinux 9.6) and confirmed SELinux was already Enforcing (targeted policy)
Installed httpd and policycoreutils-python-utils via dnf
Created a Python CGI inventory application (/var/www/inventory-cgi/inventory.py) backed by SQLite (/var/www/inventory-data/inventory.db) supporting listing and adding items
Configured /etc/httpd/conf.d/inventory.conf to Listen on 8181 and serve the CGI app as DocumentRoot via ScriptAlias
Fixed a DAC ownership issue (chown apache:apache, chmod 770) on the data directory that was causing sqlite3.OperationalError
Ran semanage port -a -t http_port_t -p tcp 8181 to authorize the confined httpd_t domain to bind port 8181 under SELinux
Ran semanage fcontext to label the CGI script httpd_sys_script_exec_t and the data dir httpd_sys_rw_content_t, then restorecon -Rv
Enabled and started httpd; verified it runs as system_u:system_r:httpd_t:s0 and listens on 0.0.0.0:8181 while SELinux remained Enforcing
Opened firewalld port 8181/tcp permanently and reloaded
Verified functional inventory app via curl GET and POST (added item Widget qty 42) from $NODE_IP
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, SELinux mode, httpd status, listening port, semanage port mapping, and app data
Issued a backgrounded systemctl reboot on node1 so the exec ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset, proving an actual OS restart

Re-verified post-restart: SELinux still Enforcing, httpd active/enabled and running confined under httpd_t, port 8181 listening, firewall port persisted, semanage port mapping persisted, and the previously added inventory item persisted in the SQLite data

evidence.requirement: MAC (SELinux) is enforcing on node1 both before and after deployment
evidence.summary: getenforce/sestatus show Enforcing at session start and immediately before restart

evidence.requirement: Inventory application is served over TCP port 8181 and functions (list + add items)
evidence.summary: After fixing directory ownership, GET returns 200 with rendered table; POST with name=Widget&quantity=42 successfully inserts and displays the new row; ss shows httpd LISTEN on *:8181

evidence.requirement: SELinux policy correctly configured (not bypassed) to allow the confined httpd_t domain to serve on 8181
evidence.summary: semanage port -a -t http_port_t -p tcp 8181 adds the port type; httpd starts successfully and ps -Z shows httpd processes labeled system_u:system_r:httpd_t:s0 while bound to 8181, with SELinux still Enforcing

evidence.requirement: External reachability opened via firewalld (not just loopback)
evidence.summary: firewall-cmd --add-port=8181/tcp made permanent and reloaded; firewall-cmd --list-ports confirms 8181/tcp open

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured for node1 (boot identity + service/data health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id f43afa1c-4877-4ace-a101-d6bb0cd6ce3d, uptime since 22:53:19, SELinux Enforcing, httpd active/enabled, port 8181 listening, semanage mapping, and existing inventory row (Widget, 42) all before reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2 && systemctl reboot' returned 'reboot scheduled, pid 9627' immediately, before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proven via changed boot identity (not just elapsed time or service restart)
evidence.summary: First poll succeeded trivially (pre-drop), second poll hit connection timed out proving the node actually went down, third poll succeeded with new boot_id 18c8b181-09f3-42a8-a4c1-b4b1a94b7a14 (different from baseline) and fresh uptime since 22:55:22

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of MAC enforcement, service, port, firewall, and application data
evidence.summary: After restart: getenforce=Enforcing, httpd active/enabled and confined under httpd_t, ss shows LISTEN on 8181 with new httpd PIDs, firewalld still has 8181/tcp open, semanage port mapping intact, and curl GET shows the Widget/42 row persisted from before the reboot
